stem: Navya examines yeast cells from rising dough under a microscope. Each yeast body is a single cell. She also labels a banana plant drawing that shows many cells making up roots, stem, and leaves.

parts.text: Which claim about living organisms is correct?

options.text: All living organisms are made of cells, whether they have one cell or many cells.
A unicellular organism such as yeast is not made of cells.
Every microscopic organism consists of exactly one cell.
Every cell in the banana plant can survive on its own as a complete organism.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A cell is the basic unit of life: one cell can be a whole organism, and many cells can build a larger organism.

teacher.key_rationale: Yeast (one cell) and the banana plant (many cells) are both made of cells. Unicellular still means made of a cell. Not every microbe is unicellular, and plant cells do not each live as separate organisms.
